question.text:
\[ A_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad A_2=\begin{bmatrix} 9 & 4 \\ -5 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \]

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $\mathcal{B}=\big\{ A_1, A_2 \big\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ A_1, A_2 \big\},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are $[C]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ A_1, A_2 \big\}$ can be written as

\begin{align*} x_1 A_1 + x_2 A_2. \end{align*}

In our case, we have

\[ [C]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, \begin{align*} C&= 4 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix} + (-1) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 4 \\ -5 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 12 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -9 & -4 \\ 5 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 & -8 \\ 5 & 9 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

In our case, we have

\[ [C]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, \begin{align*} C&= 2 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} + (-3) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 4 & -6 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -3 \\ -15 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3 \\ -11 & -6 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the polynomials $p_1(t)$ and $p_2(t),$ given by \[ p_1(t)=1+t+t^2, \qquad p_2(t)=1+t-t^2. \] Find $p(t)$ given that $\mathcal{B}=\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are $[p (t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\}$ can be written as

\begin{align*} x_1 p_1(t) + x_2 p_2(t). \end{align*}

In our case, we have

\[ [p(t) ]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align*} p(t)&= (-1) \cdot (1+t+t^2) + 1 \cdot (1+t-t^2) \\[3pt] &= -1-t-t^2+1+t-t^2 \\[3pt] &= -2t^2. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the polynomials $p_1(t)$ and $p_2(t),$ given by \[ p_1(t)=t-t^3, \qquad p_2(t)=2t^2+5t^3. \] Find $p(t)$ given that $\mathcal{B}=\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are $[p (t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\}$ can be written as

\begin{align*} x_1 p_1(t) + x_2 p_2(t). \end{align*}

In our case, we have

\[ [p(t) ]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align*} p(t)&= (-3) \cdot (t-t^3) + 1 \cdot (2t^2+5t^3) \\[3pt] &= -3t+3t^3 + 2t^2+5t^3 \\[3pt] &= -3t+2t^2+8t^3. \end{align*}

question.explanation:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\}$ can be written as

\begin{align*} x_1 p_1(t) + x_2 p_2(t). \end{align*}

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} p(t)&= 1 \cdot (1-t+2t^2) + 3 \cdot (t-t^2) \\[3pt] &= 1-t+2t^2 + 3t-3t^2 \\[3pt] &= 1+2t-t^2. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6 \\ 9 & 7 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 8 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6 \\ 9 & 7 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 8 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_2 & 6x_1+5x_2 \\ 9x_1+x_2 & 7x_1+8x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} x_2 = 2 \\ 6x_1+5x_2 = 4 \\ 9x_1+x_2 = -7 \\ 7x_1+8x_2= 9. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_3+\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)R_1 \\ R_4 :=R_4+\left(-\dfrac{7}{6}\right)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -\dfrac{13}{2} & -13 \\ 0 & \dfrac{13}{6} & \dfrac{13}{3} \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 6x_1+5x_2 = 4 \\ x_2 = 2\\ -\dfrac{13}{2}x_2= -13\\ \dfrac{13}{6}x_2= \dfrac{13}{3}. \end{cases} \] From the second, third and fourth equations, we get $x_2 =2.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} 6x_1+5\cdot 2 &= 4 \\[3pt] 6x_1 &= -6 \\[3pt] x_1 &= -1. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = -1+2=1.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -x_1 + 2x_2 & 2x_1+x_2 \\ 0 & 3x_1-x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} -x_1 + 2x_2= -10 \\ 2x_1+x_2 = 0 \\ 3x_1-x_2 = 10. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 2 & -10 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 10 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 2 & -10 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 10 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+2R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+3R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 2 & -10 \\ 0 & 5 & -20 \\ 0 & 5 & -20 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} -x_1+2x_2 = -10 \\ 5x_2 = -20\\ \end{cases} \] From the second equation, we get $x_2 =-4.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} -x_1+2\left(-4\right) &= -10 \\[3pt] -x_1 &= -2 \\[3pt] x_1 &= 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = 2 + (-4)=-2.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 2x_1 + 5x_2 & -3x_2 \\ 0 & -2x_1+4x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1+5x_2 = 4 \\ -3x_2 = -3 \\ -2x_1+4x_2 = 5. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & 5 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & 5 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_3+R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 9 & 9 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 2x_1+5x_2 = 4 \\ -3x_2 = -3\\ 9x_2= 9. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =1.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} 2x_1+5\cdot 1 &= 4 \\[3pt] 2x_1 &= -1 \\[3pt] x_1 &= -\dfrac 1 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac 1 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = -\dfrac1 2 + 1 = \dfrac 1 2.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 9 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $2x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 9 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 2x_1-2x_2 & 3x_2 \\ -x_1 & x_1+x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 9 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1-2x_2 = -2 \\ 3x_2 = 9 \\ -x_1 = -2\\ x_1+x_2 =5. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ -1 & 0 & -2\\ 1 & 1 & 5 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ -1 & 0 & -2\\ 1 & 1 & 5 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_1 \leftrightarrow R_4 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ -1 & 0 & -2\\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_3+R_1 \\ R_4 :=R_4+(-2)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\\ 0 & -4 & -12 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1+x_2 = 5 \\ 3x_2 = 9\\ x_2= 3\\ -4x_2=-12. \end{cases} \] From the second, third and fourth equations, we get $x_2 =3.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} x_1+3 &= 5 \\[3pt] x_1 &= 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $2x_1+x_2 = 2\cdot 2+3=7.$

question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 12 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 + 2x_2 & -2x_1+x_2 \\ 0 & 3x_1-3x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 12 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+2x_2 = -2 \\ -2x_1+x_2 = -6 \\ 3x_1-3x_2 = 12. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 3 & -3 & 12 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 3 & -3 & 12 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+2R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+(-3)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 0 & -9 & 18 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1+2x_2 = -2 \\ 5x_2 = -10\\ -9x_2= 18. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =-2.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} x_1+2\left(-2\right) &= -2 \\[3pt] x_1 &= 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = 2+\left(-2\right)=0.$

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials:

\[ p_1(t)=2+t, \quad p_2(t)=1-t^2, \quad q(t)=2+3t+4t^2. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t) \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (2+t)+ x_2 (1-t^2 ) &=2+3t+4t^2 \\[3pt] (2x_1+x_2)+x_1t-x_2t^2 &=2+3t+4t^2. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1+x_2 = 2 \\ x_1 = 3 \\ -x_2 = 4. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:=R_2+\left(-\dfrac1 2\right)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -\dfrac1 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 \end{array} \right] & R_3 &:=R_3+(-2)R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -\dfrac1 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1+x_2 = 2 \\ - \dfrac1 2x_2 = 2. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =-4.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ 2x_1+(-4) = 2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=3. \]

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2=3+(-4) = -1.$

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials: \[ p_1(t)=2t^2+t-2, \quad p_2(t)=t^2+3t-6, \quad p_3(t)=-2t^3+3t^2, \\[3pt] q(t)=-2t^3+4t^2+3t-6. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) , p_3(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) , p_3(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\x_3 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1, x_2$ and $x_3$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t )+x_3p_3(t) = q(t). \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (2t^2+t-2)+ x_2 (t^2+3t-6)+x_3(-2t^3+3t^2)&=-2t^3+4t^2+3t-6 \\[3pt] -2x_3t^3+(2x_1+x_2+3x_3)t^2+(x_1+3x_2)t+(-2x_1-6x_2) &= -2t^3+4t^2+3t-6. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} -2x_3 = -2 \\ 2x_1+x_2+3x_3 = 4 \\ x_1+3x_2 = 3 \\ -2x_1-6x_2 = -6. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3\\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3\\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6 \end{array} \right] && R_1 \leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2\\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+(-2)R_1 \\ R_4 := R_4 + 2R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1+3x_2 = 3 \\ -5x_2+3x_3 =-2 \\ -2x_3= -2. \end{cases} \] From the third equation, we get $x_3=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get \[ -5x_2 + 3\cdot 1 = -2 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = 1. \] Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get \[ x_1+3\cdot 1 = 3 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 0. \]

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},$ and therefore $x_2=1.$

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials:

\[ p_1(t)=2+t^2, \quad p_2(t)=1-t+2t^2, \quad q(t)=6+2t. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t) \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (2+t^2)+ x_2 (1-t+2t^2) &=6+2t \\[3pt] (2x_1+x_2)-x_2t+ (x_1+2x_2)t^2 &=6+2t. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1+x_2 = 6 \\ -x_2 = 2 \\ x_1+2x_2 = 0. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_3+\left(-\dfrac12\right)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & \dfrac32 & -3 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1 + x_2 = 6\\[3pt] x_2 = -2 \\[3pt] \dfrac3 2x_2 = -3. \end{cases} \]

From the second and third equations we get $x_2 =-2.$ Substituting this into the first equation yields

\[ 2x_1+(-2) = 6 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 4. \]

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2=4+(-2) = 2.$

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials: \[ p_1(t)=-6t^3+6t+12, \quad p_2(t)=t^3-2t^2-3t-2, \quad p_3(t)=-3t^2+2t, \\[3pt] q(t)=-9t^3+19t+18. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) , p_3(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) , p_3(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\x_3 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1, x_2$ and $x_3$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t )+x_3p_3(t) = q(t). \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (-6t^3+6t+12)+ x_2 (t^3-2t^2-3t-2)+x_3(-3t^2+2t)&=-9t^3+19t+18 \\[3pt] (-6x_1+x_2)t^3+(-2x_2-3x_3)t^2+(6x_1-3x_2+2x_3)t+(12x_1-2x_2) &= -9t^3+19t+18. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} -6x_1+x_2 = -9 \\ -2x_2-3x_3 = 0 \\ 6x_1-3x_2+2x_3 = 19 \\ 12x_1-2x_2 = 18. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 2 & 19 \\ 12 & -2 & 0 & 18 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 2 & 19 \\ 12 & -2 & 0 & 18 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_3+R_1 \\ R_4 :=R_4+2R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 10\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_3+(-1)R_2 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 10\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} -6x_1+x_2 = -9 \\ -2x_2-3x_3 =0\\ 5x_3= 10. \end{cases} \] From the third equation, we get $x_3=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get \[ -2x_2-3\cdot 2 = 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = -3. \] Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get \[ -6x_1+(-3) = -9 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 1. \]

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix},$ and therefore $x_2=-3.$

Consider the following polynomials: \[ p_1(t)=-t^3+t^2+t, \quad p_2(t)=2t^2+4, \quad p_3(t)=3t^3-t^2-3t+3, \\[3pt] q(t)=-1. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) , p_3(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) , p_3(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\x_3 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_3=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1, x_2$ and $x_3$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t )+x_3p_3(t) = q(t). \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (-t^3+t^2+t)+ x_2 (2t^2+4 )+x_3(3t^3-t^2-3t+3)&=-1 \\[3pt] (-x_1+3x_3)t^3+(x_1+2x_2-x_3)t^2+(x_1-3x_3)t+(4x_2+3x_3) &= -1. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} -x_1+3x_3 = 0 \\ x_1+2x_2-x_3 = 0 \\ x_1-3x_3 = 0 \\ 4x_2+3x_3 = -1. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 0\\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -1 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 0\\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -1 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -1 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_4+(-2)R_2 \end{array}\\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 \leftrightarrow R_4 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} -x_1+3x_3 = 0 \\ 2x_2+2x_3 =0\\ -x_3= -1. \end{cases} \] From the third equation, we get $x_3=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get \[ 2x_2+2\cdot 1 = 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = -1. \] Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get \[ -x_1+3\cdot 1 = 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 3. \]

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},$ and therefore $x_3=1.$
